newsitem.title: USA: STAAR Surgical comfortable with estimates.
newsitem.headline: STAAR Surgical comfortable with estimates.

text.p: John Wolf, President and Chief Executive Officer of STARR Surgical Co, said Monday he is comfortable with analysts' earnings expectations of $0.13 a share in the fourth quarter and $0.64 a share in fiscal 1997.
"We're pretty much in agreement with (earnings estimates)," Wolf said in an interview, adding that if all went well, Staar could beat those numbers by about five percent.
Wolf said he sees sales growing in some European countries, China, other parts of Asia, Australia and South America.

"There is a very good chance that in the first quarter we will begin to see an increase in sales in some of our newer technologies, including implantable contact lenses and our glaucoma draining device," he said.
U.S. clinical trials of the company's implantable contact lenses and glaucoma draining device are set to start in the first quarter of 1997.
Wolf said he sees revenues in fiscal 1997 of about $52 million and sees $67 million the following year.

He said the increase in 1998 sales will be helped by STAAR's Hyaluronic Acid and Toric Intraoccular lens products, which he hopes will both get U.S. Food and Drug Administration approval sometime in 1997.

Earlier STARR reported third quarter earnings of $1.7 million, or $0.13 a share, on revenues of $10.8 million. Last year STAAR recorded third quarter profits of $2.1 million, or $0.16 a share, on revenues of $8.9 million.

The fall-off in profits was due in large part to a change in accounting procedures that saw the company pay a 33 percent year-to-date tax rate compared with nominal tax in the previous year. Pretax earnings for the latest quarter were $0.20 a share compared with $0.16 in the year-ago period.
With headquarters in Monrovia, Calif., STAAR develops, makes and distributes medical devices used in minimally invasive ophthalmic surgery.
